chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from al-Abbas ibn Amir from Dawud ibn Husayn from Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked about a man who made a will, and his heirs were the witnesses, so they validated it for him. When the man died, they annulled it. Is it for them to reject what they had acknowledged? He said: 'It is not for them to do so; the will is binding upon them if they acknowledged it during his lifetime.'
ai.seo_question: Can heirs annul a will if they witnessed and validated it while the testator was alive?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in inheritance law: once heirs validate the will during the testator's life, their subsequent repudiation is invalid. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the binding nature of mutual consent (*iqrar*) among heirs, ensuring stability in estate distribution and preventing arbitrary revocation of agreed-upon bequests.
